Rekindling the Verdant Years Chapter 68: Sorry, I Already Like Someone

Although Kong Junxiang said yesterday that we only had to be in the classroom before eight this morning.

But most students still arrived at the classroom one after another before seven.

When Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng walked in through the back door of the classroom, it was already more than half full.

"Zhu Yufei, call a few people over." When Li Luo passed by Zhu Yufei, he patted him on the shoulder, which made him jump.

Li Luo looked down with a puzzled expression, only to find that the kid was secretly playing on his phone.

"Class monitor, you scared me to death." Zhu Yufei turned his head and saw it was Li Luo, looking speechless. "I thought it was Teacher Kong."

"What are you playing?" Li Luo leaned in curiously to take a look and found the kid was actually reading a webnovel. "What book is this?"

"I'm Really Not a Star, it's pretty good." Zhu Yufei secretly showed it to Li Luo. "The main character is dating three female celebrities, it's so thrilling."

"Thrilling my ass, he hasn't even bedded one yet." Zhang Guohuang, who was next to him, complained, "The main character is a total eunuch."

Li Luo: "...Where are you two reading this?"

"Some-pavilion, of course."

"Oh." Li Luo nodded, walked back to his seat with a straight face, and put down his schoolbag. "You'd better put your phone away, don't let Teacher Kong find it."

"Don't worry, don't worry. When it comes to a battle of wits with the teacher, I'm very experienced in this." Zhu Yufei winked at him, then got up and called a few boys over. "We're going to get the school uniforms, right?"

"Right." Li Luo replied, silently suppressing the urge to assassinate the two of them, and led the team out the door. "To the warehouse by the sports field."

...

In the morning, Li Luo led some people to pick up the school uniforms for Class 8, two sets per person, and distributed them to everyone.

At eight-thirty, the school placement test officially began. The first subject was Chinese.

Mathematics was at one in the afternoon, followed by English at three, and that was it.

Because middle school's politics, history, and science would become six elective subjects in high school, they were not included in this placement test, which focused solely on the three main subjects.

For Li Luo, this was some relatively good news.

After all, Chinese and English were heavily influenced by his memory palace. Even if he didn't know the test questions in advance, his scores wouldn't be much worse than they were on the high school entrance exam.

But for subjects like mathematics and science, he was in deep trouble.

However, it was just a placement test. Li Luo wasn't too concerned about the score. As long as he studied hard after school started, with the ability of his memory palace, if he still couldn't learn well, he might as well just find a block of tofu and bash his head against it.

In the past few days, apart from attending classes seriously after the tests were over, Li Luo's remaining energy was mainly focused on his daily writing and the recording of those two songs.

However, there was still a problem...

"Your singing... has quite a few problems."

The day after the placement test, on Tuesday, Yan Zhusheng and Li Luo snuck into an empty classroom on the sixth floor to practice singing during the lunch break.

Because of Yan Zhusheng's high standards for songs, Li Luo had been practicing according to her criteria for the past two days.

To be honest, his singing level was definitely considered pretty good among ordinary people, but compared to a professional like Yan Zhusheng, it was like heaven and earth.

"So how long do I have to practice?" Li Luo asked with a helpless look. "Aren't many singers studio gods? Can't you just touch it up for me then?"

"It's always better if it's natural," Yan Zhusheng said. "Besides, singing skills need to be practiced and improved slowly. If you start practicing now, you definitely won't see any major improvement by this weekend, but it will accumulate over time, and the progress will be very obvious in the future."

"Alright then." Li Luo sighed, then said, "But for that song, Annulus, just record your version. I'll only record Waiting for You After Class."

Yan Zhusheng didn't ask why. Hearing him say this, she just nodded and said, "Okay, but I have another problem here."

"What?"

"This song of yours, Annulus, what is it about?" Yan Zhusheng tilted her head and asked. "Sadness, regret, a sense of pity?"

"Uh... just sing it like a sad love song, it's more or less the same meaning."

"But what I'm worst at are sad love songs." Yan Zhusheng frowned.

Reminded by Yan Zhusheng, Li Luo suddenly realized.

Even ten years later, the short video songs that Yan Zhusheng posted online were often commented on by netizens as being from a "soulless vocal-flexing machine."

When it came to singing those more rousing songs that required a bright timbre to power through the climax, she could still use the quality of her tone to cover up this issue.

But when it came to love songs that required a gentle and tender touch, Yan Zhusheng wasn't quite up to the task.

She could sing them, but it just didn't have that feel.

But Li Luo, in essence, didn't require Yan Zhusheng to sing it perfectly.

After all, her skill was undeniable. Li Luo just needed the song Annulus to add some flavor to the webnovel he was writing.

He was also quite curious himself: if a song that was originally a massive hit was created in an entertainment-themed novel, could it still become as popular as it originally was?

He also wondered how much money this song could sell for under these circumstances.

"However," Yan Zhusheng said suddenly, "there is another way for me to sing a sad love song."

"What way?" Li Luo was taken aback and asked curiously.

Yan Zhusheng tilted her head slightly, looked at Li Luo, and after thinking for a moment, suddenly said to him, "I like you."

Li Luo felt his heart skip a beat. "...Huh?"

"You have to reject me." Yan Zhusheng furrowed her brow and even began to earnestly discuss it with Li Luo, "I've read some novels where the female protagonist feels terrible after her feelings are thwarted. I need to find that kind of feeling."

The corner of Li Luo's mouth twitched. He thought, what kind of unorthodox method is this, and couldn't help but ask, "What kind of method do you call this?"

"Situational immersion?" Yan Zhusheng blinked. "Anyway, let's give it a try."

"Fine." Li Luo swallowed, suddenly sitting up straight with a more serious expression. "Go ahead, I'm ready."

"Okay." Seeing how serious he was, Yan Zhusheng also composed herself, took a deep breath, and then looked at him again. "Li Luo, I like you."

To be honest.

Even if it was fake, being confessed to by a girl like Yan Zhusheng still made one's heart race.

The midday sun slanted in through the window, falling on Yan Zhusheng's side profile. Light and shadow intertwined perfectly on her fair face.

It made one subconsciously hold their breath.

Li Luo averted his gaze and said with difficulty, "Sorry, I already like someone."

Hearing his words, Yan Zhusheng quietly closed her eyes.

She picked up the guitar beside her, her fingers slowly strumming the strings.

In her mind, she tried hard to recall various heart-wrenching scenes she had once seen, combining them with the feeling of just being rejected, and as the emotions surged, Yan Zhusheng pursed her lips lightly, with a hint of bitterness:

"A circle is drawn into a fingerprint~"

"Imprinted on my lips~"

Li Luo, who was standing opposite her, was stunned for a moment. Feeling the subtle emotions contained in the lyrics, he was a little surprised.

No way... it actually works?

Shelving Announcement

Rekindling the Verdant Years Shelving Announcement

1. Shelving Time

This book will be officially shelved at midnight on June 1st.

That is, in 2 hours.

I hope everyone can show their support.

Or2

----------

2. Source of Inspiration

Readers who have read "Senpai, Stop Talking!" might still have some impression.

In chapter 337 of that book, the protagonist, Jiang Miao, as a webnovel author, wrote a new book called "My Tenants Are a Bit Strange."

That can be considered the most primitive first draft of this book, "Rekindling the Verdant Years."

As for the idea itself, it was recorded in my inspiration bank as early as January 2022.

Originally, before writing "Rebirth: Swimming Against the Current for Ten Years," I had considered directly writing this current novel that starts from high school.

Because I had already written two consecutive books with a university setting, I was somewhat fatigued.

But since it was my first time trying to write multiple female leads and my first time properly writing a career plotline, my thought at the time was to write a practice novel first.

I would save the high school plot I wanted to write for later, when I was confident I could handle it.

With this thought in mind, "Swimming Against the Current for Ten Years" was born.

It was written by me in a hurry, following the standard template of a rebirth novel. The female leads' names were originally going to be "Yan Zhusheng" and "Xu Youyu."

But I like these two names very much and was reluctant to use them in an experimental work, so I changed them to two other names at the last minute.

Yan Chicu is simply a homophone for "being jealous" (chi cu).

Xu Niannian was taken from the "niannian" in "niannian you yu" (may you have abundance year after year).

And the "Xu Youyu" in this book uses the meaning from both "niannian you yu" and "giving a man a fish is not as good as teaching him how to fish" (shou ren yi yu, buru shou ren yi yu).

After more than two years, I'm finally able to write this story, and I'm very happy about it.

----------

3. Content of This Book

A long time ago, I thought that I must write a rebirth novel with a high school theme in the future.

The protagonist's goal after rebirth is no longer to aim for Tencent, Alibaba, or ByteDance, but to focus on daily life.

Occasionally using the forward-looking perspective of a reincarnator to earn a little money, taking advantage of information gaps to make some profit, just enough to earn the money needed for this life.

The remaining time would be spent squandering it, enjoying it, truly and personally experiencing a high school and university life without any worries for the future.

Sometimes I see comments from some readers saying things like "you can buy Bitcoin," "why not play the stock market?" "buy the lottery!" and so on.

Or some comments saying "it's already 2014, all the various sectors have been occupied by capital, there are no opportunities left."

I can understand your feelings, but after reading many rebirth novels, I don't know if another thought has ever occurred to you.

The protagonist's money is ultimately just a number; no matter how much is earned, it won't end up in our hands.

Anyway, after being reborn, they can make money one way or another. I'm more interested in seeing how the protagonist treats his own life after rebirth.

Crushing Alibaba and Tencent in business, having all sorts of beauties fall into his arms in love, achieving a double harvest in career and relationships, and reaching the pinnacle of life.

I have read many rebirth novels like this.

They are very satisfying, very stress-relieving.

But I've tried it before, and with my personality, I probably can't write this type of story well.

That's why this current book, "Rekindling the Verdant Years," exists.

In the summary of this book, I wrote several tags.

Rebirth, High School, Campus, Slice-of-Life, Light Entertainment Industry

This should effectively summarize the core content and highlights of this book.

There is no "romance" in it.

Because if the words "romance" and "high school" appear in the summary at the same time, it's easy to get reported and blocked.

And it's true that I haven't written any "romance" at the moment, have I?

What I've written is just the budding feelings and subconscious desires for affection in the hearts of teenage boys and girls during puberty.

I chatted with a friend about this before, and he joked, "How is this multiple female leads? This is no female lead, right? How can high school students be in a relationship? They are all just good friends!"

Of course, this is just a joke.

In fact, when I recall my memories from junior high and high school, there are many beautiful and innocent things.

Looking back with a mature perspective now, there are many things where I can't even figure out why my choices at the time were what they were.

Ignorant and clueless.

But that's what youth is, isn't it?

Just like when I was writing "Liu Shaowen" and "Shao Heqi," I actually don't dislike them. On the contrary, I find them a bit "adorable."

Are the two of them simps?

Yes, and no.

Because they are genuinely adorable, with their heartstrings plucked by the throbbing of youthful infatuation in their hearts.

I've even done some stupid things myself, just not as exaggerated as in the book.

And now, at 26 years old, I probably can't find that feeling anymore.

Now when I see a beautiful woman, my mind only thinks "so pretty, want to f*ck," and I no longer hold any hope or expectation for so-called love.

Writing this book is like reminiscing and commemorating my own dead youth.

And by the way, I'll light an incense stick for all of your youths as well.

If any of you are still in school, then cherish the present moment. I wish that you can still feel this throb.

----------

① Using 3,000 first-day subscriptions as the baseline, for every additional 100 subscriptions above that, a bonus chapter will be added. The first-day subscription data will be based on my后台 data at midnight on the day after shelving.

② Using the average subscription data on the day after shelving as a baseline, from then until the end of June, for every 100-point increase in average subscriptions, a bonus chapter will be added.

③ Based on the monthly tickets in June, for every 500 monthly tickets, a bonus chapter will be added.

④ A "Leader" level donation gets one bonus chapter (please donate within your means, don't force it, especially student readers. Being able to support with official subscriptions is already great).

⑤ A guaranteed minimum of 4,000 words updated daily. For any words exceeding 4,000, every 2,000 words counts as one bonus chapter.

Example: For a certain day's update, the first chapter is 2,400 words, the second is 2,300 words, and the third is 3,300 words. The total word count for that day is 8,000 words. After subtracting the guaranteed 4,000 words, there are an additional 4,000 words, which counts as two bonus chapters.

The above rules are only effective for June.
